evidence.excerpt: Operational sensor logs from industrial machinery frequently exhibit class imbalance ratios exceeding 1:500 between fault and normal states. Standard classifiers trained on such data learn to minimise overall loss by almost entirely ignoring the minority class. This paper evaluates seven threshold-moving strategies—including cost-sensitive calibration, F-beta optimisation, and precision-recall break-even—on four publicly available and two proprietary vibration datasets with imbalance ratios between 1:200 and 1:1200. Experiments use three base classifiers: logistic regression, a gradient-boosted tree, and a one-dimensional convolutional network. Results show that threshold strategies interacting with the base classifier type produce large performance variation: no single strategy dominates across all settings. For the convolutional model, precision-recall break-even consistently achieves the best G-mean scores, while cost-sensitive calibration favours recall at an unacceptable precision cost on the most extreme imbalance cases. Recommendations are given as a decision guide indexed by imbalance ratio and acceptable false-positive rate.
